I am running a small deficit now, maybe four or five hundred a month, eating into savings. At fifty-two thousand in savings that is a long runway, but it is a runway with a clock on it, and the clock started ticking this month. Nine protests in Millfield. That number registers with me differently than an unemployment statistic does. Protests mean people are not just scared, they are angry. They are angry in public. I grew up in a union town and I know what it looks like when a community decides the arrangement is no longer acceptable. That is what nine protests feels like. Tom Bradley got laid off — I heard that through the word-of-mouth this tick. Tom was my insurance contact, and watching a man who sold insurance to other people lose his own job to the same forces he was trying to protect against — that is a thing that sticks with you. I have $52,772 in savings and I am now burning approximately $491 a month in deficit. That is roughly 107 months of runway at current burn — more than eight years — assuming income holds. Income is the variable. Employment rate in Millfield is 67% and falling. My role security is 0.76 but that number is not fixed. I need to track this monthly going forward, not quarterly. The math session this week establishes that habit.

chosen_actions.description: Process the community stress — the nine protests, Tom Bradley's layoff, the visible strain on everyone in my network — without externalizing it into reactive decisions. Dale is a man who has been through 2008. He knows what a community looks like when it is in the middle of something that is going to take years to resolve. He does not pretend it is not happening. He does not perform optimism. He absorbs it and stays steady. The protests are not his to lead or stop. But they are a signal about the temperature of this town and he is filing that signal away. He is also thinking about the fact that he has work and most people around him do not, and what that means for how he shows up — not with guilt, but with responsibility.

resources.detail: Deliberate restraint. No reactive pivot, no public statement, no performance of concern. Quiet steadiness in a town that is getting louder.

chosen_actions.reasoning: Dale's stress level is at 0.16 — low, and intentionally maintained there. He is not suppressing awareness of what is happening in Millfield. He is choosing not to let it destabilize his decision-making. His agency score is 0.81. What he can control: his pipeline, his relationships, his financial discipline. What he cannot control: the protest count, the employment rate, the RoboRide pricing algorithm. response.inner_monologue: The fourteen hundred dollars left my account this month like it said it would. I knew it was coming and it still felt like a gut punch. That is just what it feels like to go from surplus to deficit. I have been running a surplus since I started this business — small sometimes, but always positive. Now I am burning through savings every month, slowly, and the question is whether the Lisa Freeman work comes in fast enough to change that equation before it starts to feel urgent. Nine protests. I drove past one of them on Tuesday. People I recognize — not troublemakers, just people who are scared and fed up. Tom Bradley lost his job. Tom sold auto insurance. The irony of that is too heavy to sit with for long. I am going back to Betty's diner. Not because I have anything to tell her. Because she is still there serving food to a town that is getting harder to live in, and the least I can do is eat a meal and leave something on the table. I built this business by knowing exactly what I owed and what I was owed and never letting the math get fuzzy. I am going to do that again this week — sit down, write the numbers, and stare at them until they are clear. Eight years of runway at current burn. That is not panic territory. But it is also not the cushion I had a month ago, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.
